Physics Course Plan

Overall Philosophy

The plan will prioritize conceptual understanding over rote memorization, with an emphasis on practical application and problem-solving. Regular review and reinforcement will be incorporated to solidify learning.

Eight-Week Course Schedule

Week 1-2: Simple Harmonics & Waves (12 hours)

Topics

  • Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM)
  • Wave Properties (transverse, longitudinal)
  • Wave Speed, Frequency, Wavelength
  • Superposition

Activities

  • Demonstrations of SHM (pendulum, spring)
  • Wave simulations
  • Problem-solving exercises relating wave properties

Algebraic Focus

  • Equations relating wave speed, frequency, and wavelength (v = fλ)
  • Introduction to the concept of amplitude

Week 3-4: Wave Functions & Light and Sound (12 hours)

Topics

  • Wave Functions (mathematical representation)
  • Interference
  • Diffraction
  • Doppler Effect
  • Speed of Sound
  • Intensity of Sound

Activities

  • Graphical representation of wave functions
  • Simulations demonstrating interference and diffraction
  • Calculations involving the Doppler Effect

Algebraic Focus

  • Basic trigonometric functions (sine, cosine) in wave representation

Week 5: Electromagnetism (12 hours)

Topics

  • Introduction to Electric and Magnetic Fields
  • Relationship between Electricity and Magnetism
  • Electromagnetic Spectrum

Activities

  • Demonstrations of magnetic fields
  • Discussions on electromagnetic radiation properties

Algebraic Focus

  • Qualitative understanding of electric and magnetic field relationships

Week 6-7: Electrostatics (12 hours)

Topics

  • Electric Charge
  • Coulomb’s Law
  • Electric Field
  • Electric Potential
  • Capacitance

Activities

  • Demonstrations of electrostatic forces
  • Calculations involving Coulomb’s Law and electric potential

Algebraic Focus

  • Coulomb’s Law (F = k q1 q2 / r^2)
  • Electric potential (V = k q / r)
  • Equation for capacitance (C = Q/V)

Week 8: Electrical Current (12 hours)

Topics

  • Electric Current
  • Ohm’s Law
  • Resistance
  • Series and Parallel Circuits
  • Kirchhoff’s Laws

Activities

  • Circuit building exercises
  • Calculations involving Ohm’s Law and Kirchhoff’s Laws

Algebraic Focus

  • Ohm’s Law (V = IR)
  • Equations for equivalent resistance in series and parallel circuits

Review and Reinforcement

Throughout the eight weeks, regular review sessions will be incorporated to reinforce key concepts. Problem-solving exercises will be assigned to provide students with opportunities to apply their knowledge.

Bridging the Units

Waves to Electromagnetism

Emphasize the wave nature of light and its relationship to electric and magnetic fields.

Electromagnetism to Electrostatics

Highlight the connection between oscillating electric fields and the behavior of charges.

Electrostatics to Electrical Current

Demonstrate how the movement of charges in an electric field creates an electric current.

Detailed Outline

I. Simple Harmonics & Waves (Weeks 1 & 2)

(a) Lectures

  • Introduction to Periodic Motion & SHM
  • Mathematical Description of SHM (position, velocity, acceleration)
  • Wave Properties: Transverse vs. Longitudinal
  • Wave Speed, Frequency, and Wavelength
  • Superposition and Interference

(b) Problem Sets

  • SHM calculations (period, frequency, energy)
  • Wave speed and wavelength problems
  • Superposition and interference scenarios

(c) Giancoli Chapters

  • 14.1 - 14.7, 15.1 - 15.4

(d) Labs/Datasets

  • Pendulum Period vs. Length (data collection and analysis)
  • Standing Waves on a String (measurement of wavelengths and frequencies)

(e) Quizzes

  • Conceptual (SHM characteristics)
  • Computational (wave speed calculations)

(f) Unit Assessment

Combination of conceptual and computational problems.

II. Wave Functions & Light and Sound (Week 3 & 4)

(a) Lectures

  • Mathematical Representation of Waves (wave functions)
  • Interference of Waves (constructive and destructive)
  • Diffraction of Waves
  • Doppler Effect (for sound)
  • Speed of Sound and Intensity

(b) Problem Sets

  • Wave function calculations
  • Interference patterns
  • Doppler Effect calculations

(c) Giancoli Chapters

  • 15.5 - 15.8, 17.1 - 17.4

(d) Labs/Datasets

  • Young’s Double Slit Experiment (qualitative observation)
  • Analysis of Sound Intensity Data

(e) Quizzes

  • Conceptual (wave interference)
  • Computational (Doppler Effect)

(f) Unit Assessment

Application of wave principles to real-world scenarios.

III. Electromagnetism (Week 5)

(a) Lectures

  • Electric and Magnetic Fields – Qualitative Introduction
  • Relationship between Electricity and Magnetism (brief overview)
  • The Electromagnetic Spectrum

(b) Problem Sets

Conceptual exercises linking electricity and magnetism.

(c) Giancoli Chapters

  • 26.1 - 26.3 (selective reading)

(d) Labs/Datasets

Demonstration of magnetic fields with compasses and magnets.

(e) Quizzes

Conceptual (EM spectrum)

(f) Unit Assessment

Short answer questions on the relationship between electricity and magnetism.

IV. Electrostatics (Weeks 6 & 7)

(a) Lectures

  • Electric Charge and Coulomb’s Law
  • Electric Field
  • Electric Potential
  • Capacitance

(b) Problem Sets

  • Coulomb’s Law calculations
  • Electric field calculations
  • Capacitance calculations

(c) Giancoli Chapters

  • 22.1 - 22.5, 23.1 - 23.3

(d) Labs/Datasets

Electrostatic Force Measurement (qualitative)

(e) Quizzes

  • Conceptual (electric field)
  • Computational (Coulomb’s Law)

(f) Unit Assessment

Problem-solving involving electric fields and potential.

V. Electrical Current (Week 8)

(a) Lectures

  • Electric Current and Ohm’s Law
  • Resistance
  • Series and Parallel Circuits
  • Kirchhoff’s Laws

(b) Problem Sets

  • Ohm’s Law calculations
  • Circuit analysis (series and parallel)

(c) Giancoli Chapters

  • 20.1 - 20.5, 20.7 - 20.9

(d) Labs/Datasets

Circuit building and analysis.

(e) Quizzes

  • Conceptual (Ohm’s Law)
  • Computational (circuit analysis)

(f) Unit Assessment

Comprehensive problem-solving on circuits.
